sources.citation: The Word for the World International & The Word for the World Nigeria. 2025. Mata [The Gospel According to Matthew in the Basa-Gurmana language of Nigeria; USFM id line 'MAT- Bassa (akwaromba)']. eBible.org digital edition, id buj / BUJTWF, CC BY-SA 4.0, last updated 2025-07-12. 28 chapters (USFM, HTML, ePub, PDF, plain text).
sources.note: No linguistic front matter at all (copyright/licence page only). The practical orthography marks neither tone nor stress: a census of the whole book finds a single combining diacritic, COMBINING MACRON BELOW (4,460 tokens, on vowels, e.g. ka̱hin, iwa̱re, natosuwa̱), evidently a vowel-quality mark, and no acute/grave/circumflex/caron anywhere. Useful as the first open text corpus of Kɔrɔmba (c. 144k characters) and as evidence that an orthography decision was taken c. 2025 (TWFTW Nigeria), which implies unpublished orthography/phonology notes may exist with the translators.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart. 2012. The Kainji languages. Report prepared for the 'Towards Proto-Niger-Congo: comparison and reconstruction' project (LLACAN, Paris), School of Oriental and African Studies, dated 30 August 2012. 6 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 1.3 'Linguistic features' gives family-wide notes only: 6- or 8-vowel systems with the mid-high central vowel, vowel-harmony types, implosives/labiovelars, syllable structure from CV-only (Kambari) to complex clusters (C'Lela), and 'in Sengwe [nouns] are more often monosyllabic with a correspondingly more complex tonal inventory'; utterance-final devoicing in Kamuku and Shiroro languages. Nothing on stress; nothing specific to Basa-Gurmana or the Basa cluster.
